To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) dugongs feed in proportion to the availability of seagrass species; 2) the biomass of each segrass species is the most important factor determining consumption; 3) species composition and/or nutrient content influences consumption to a lesser extent.

Dugongs consume seagrass species available at a site in proportion to their abundance and that biomass is the primary determinant of seagrass consumption, with species composition and/or nutrient content having a secondary influence.
